moat_against: Sports rights are rented, not owned — renewal costs escalate, leagues hold leverage
Cord-cutting shrinks the linear cable/broadcast distribution base secularly
Event cyclicality: Super Bowl / elections / World Cup rotate, making OE lumpy
Announced Roku acquisition adds integration, price and leverage risk
Murdoch family control / governance concentration; news-brand advertiser and litigation exposure
moat_for: Fox News: #1 cable news, loyal engaged audience, affiliate-fee pricing power
Scarce live sports rights (NFL to 2033, MLB, college, soccer) — must-carry, DVR-proof
Tubi scale in free AVOD streaming — 110M MAU, record Q4 FY26 revenue
Live news/sports mix is resilient to time-shifting and subscription fatigue
moat_justification: Moderate-strong (6/10): Fox News is the top-rated US cable news network with a loyal, highly engaged audience and proven affiliate-fee pricing power, and live sports rights (NFL through 2033, MLB, college football, marquee soccer) are scarce, DVR-proof inventory distributors must carry. Tubi adds scale in free ad-supported streaming (110M monthly active users at FY2026 close, record revenue quarter in Q4 FY26). Against that, the core content is rented not owned — sports rights reprice upward at renewal and leagues keep the leverage — the linear distribution base shrinks secularly with cord-cutting, the audience/event calendar is cyclical (Super Bowl, elections, World Cup rotate through Fox years), and the announced Roku acquisition would materially change the risk and leverage profile. Real pricing power in news/sports, but no durable ownership of the underlying rights.
name: Fox Corporation
one_liner: Quality live news/sports cash generator, moat 6/10, but at $62.21 it does not clear 15% — weighted IRR 10.4%, weighted IV@15% $37.43; it would need to trade near $37 to clear the 15% hurdle.
